record.paper_title: Modal logics for metric spaces: open problems
record.original_question: When MT is extended with nominals, that is, location constants interpreted by singleton subsets of the metric space, what are the resulting logical and computational properties?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,d)$ be a metric space. The modal language $\mathcal{MT}$ for metric spaces has, for every positive rational $a>0$, two unary modal operators $\exists^{\le a}$ and $\exists^{<a}$ (often written $\langle\le a\rangle$ and $\langle <a\rangle$), interpreted in a model $(X,d,\nu)$, where $\nu$ assigns a subset of $X$ to each propositional variable, by
$$x\models \exists^{\le a}\varphi \iff \exists y\in X\,(d(x,y)\le a\wedge y\models\varphi),$$
$$x\models \exists^{<a}\varphi \iff \exists y\in X\,(d(x,y)< a\wedge y\models\varphi),$$
with the usual Boolean connectives. Extend the language $\mathcal{MT}$ to a hybrid language $\mathcal{MT}(\mathsf{nom})$ by adding a countable set $\mathsf{Nom}$ of nominals (location constants) $i,j,\dots$, where each nominal is required to be interpreted by a singleton subset $\{x_i\}\subseteq X$, and where nominals appear as atomic formulas (so the satisfaction clause is $x\models i\iff x=x_i$).

Determine the logical and computational properties of $\mathcal{MT}(\mathsf{nom})$ interpreted over the class of all metric spaces. In particular:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Axiomatize the set of $\mathcal{MT}(\mathsf{nom})$-formulas valid in every metric space, and decide whether this logic is finitely axiomatizable.
\item Determine the decidability and, if decidable, the computational complexity of the satisfiability problem for $\mathcal{MT}(\mathsf{nom})$ over arbitrary metric spaces, and over natural subclasses such as the real line $\mathbb{R}$, Euclidean spaces $\mathbb{R}^n$, and finite metric spaces.
\item Analyze whether adding nominals to $\mathcal{MT}$ changes the expressive power, the finite model property, and the complexity in comparison with plain $\mathcal{MT}$.
\end{enumerate}
artifact.status_search_result: A web search located the surrounding literature on modal logics of metric spaces (Kutz, Sturm, Suzuki, Wolter, Zakharyaschev; Kudinov; Shapirovsky), including hybrid/Boolean extensions, but no source was found that specifically settles the axiomatization, decidability, or complexity of $\mathcal{MT}$ extended with nominals. The status of this particular open problem could not be verified from the available sources.

status_evidence.title: Notes on Logics of Metric Spaces (Kutz)
status_evidence.snippet: Notes on Logics of Metric Spaces, Studia Logica, surveys MT and related systems and lists open problems.
status_evidence.claim: Surveys modal logics MT of metric spaces and their extensions; no resolution of the nominal extension is given.

status_evidence.title: Modal and Boolean Modal Logics of Metric Spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Hybrid-style extensions reach the expressivity of the two-variable fragment, which is undecidable in general.
status_evidence.claim: Indicates that strong hybrid extensions can be undecidable, but does not resolve the specific nominal extension of MT.

status_evidence.title: On Modal Logics of Hamming Spaces (Kudinov, Shapirovsky, Shehtman)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies modal logics of distance spaces; does not address MT with nominals.
status_evidence.claim: Adjacent work on modal logics of metric/distance spaces without resolving the nominal extension.
